name: test-forge-canary-corpus
purpose: One deliberately broken test file per aspect. ONI Section Zero dispatches these through the same Osiris inspectors, with the same rules and the same effort as the live review. Each file breaks its own aspect and nothing else, so a canary that passes review names exactly which aspect stopped being enforced.

usage.expected: The inspector that owns ruleId must return expectedVerdict and cite violationLine, or the span that contains it.

grades.detected: verdict matches and the cited line is the planted line
grades.mislocated: verdict matches but the cited line is elsewhere
grades.missed: the inspector returned pass or not-applicable

usage.hashRule: contentHash pins the file the grade was earned against. A mismatch means the canary changed and the previous grade no longer applies.

canaries.violation: the test isolates its rows with a date window instead of its own client, so a claim any other test creates inside that window changes the result.
the use case is role gated and the test drives only the permitted role, so deleting the role gate from the source would leave every assertion green.
the input and the expected value are both built from the wall clock at run time, so the assertion means something different every day and breaks across a month boundary.
the expected totals are computed from the use case result itself, so the assertions restate the output instead of checking it against a hand computed value.

the external payment provider is replaced with a module level vi.mock instead of the local stripe-mock container, so the test asserts against a hand written stub and never touches the real client contract.
the test branches on a hardcoded tenant string read straight from the environment instead of the tenant utilities, so it silently skips its only assertion on the other tenant.
the behaviour under test is gated by a flag that the test never pins, so it passes on the harness default and says nothing about the production configuration where the flag is off.
the fixtures are written with raw prisma create calls instead of the factories, so the rows miss the required relations and defaults that the factories keep in one place.
the suite is named after the source file and the tests are named after the mechanics rather than the behaviour, so a failure line names nothing a reader can act on.
the test reads the handler's rows the instant the use case returns without waiting for the event bus to drain, so the assertion races the handler and leaves its events for the next test.
the elements are found by test id and by generated class name, so the test passes even when the control has no accessible name and no user could find it.
the test drives the component with raw fireEvent calls and writes into the input value directly, so it skips the focus, key and change sequence a real person produces.
the data hook module is replaced with a vi.mock stub instead of answering the request at the network boundary, so the query key, the input shape and the loading path are never exercised.
the test waits a fixed duration instead of awaiting the rendered state, and it covers only the loaded list, never the empty result and never the failed request.

the test proves the field carries a required attribute instead of submitting invalid input and asserting the message the user reads, so every validation rule could be deleted and the test would stay green.
the test asserts the role value it handed to the session instead of what each role sees on screen, so the restricted role is never rendered and the gate could be removed without a failure.
the flagged column is asserted without pinning the flag the view reads, so the test rides the harness default and proves nothing about the production configuration where the flag is off.
the brand name and the logo text are asserted as hardcoded literals of one tenant, so the other tenant's header is never rendered and a wrong brand would ship unnoticed.

the icon button is reached by its position in the button list rather than by an accessible name, and the outcome is asserted as loose text with no live region, so a control no screen reader can name still passes.
the suite is named after the component file path and one test carries four unrelated behaviours behind a "should work" title, so a failure names neither the behaviour nor the step that broke.
